summary.headline: Petronet posted record quarterly PBT of INR 1,795 crore and PAT of INR 1,338 crore in Q4 FY26, but Dahej utilisation fell to about 53% in March amid the Gulf supply disruption.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered the highest quarterly PBT and PAT in company history, with PBT up from INR 1,144 crore QoQ and PAT up to INR 1,338 crore from INR 848 crore, helped by a one-off UOP reversal. Volumes fell QoQ to 219 TBTU, with Dahej utilisation at 90.1% for the quarter but only about 53% in March after Qatari cargoes stopped. Management said April and May utilisation remained at the March level, and recovery depends on the Gulf conflict ending and Qatar resuming supply within 3 to 4 weeks. FY27 capex is guided at about INR 9,000 crore, mainly the petchem project, and the dividend is to be maintained.

segments.name: Dahej terminal
segments.commentary: Q4 throughput 201 TBTU at 90.1% utilisation, but March fell to about 53%. Regas revenue from third parties was INR 879 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Kochi terminal
segments.commentary: Achieved its highest-ever annual throughput of 68 TBTU in FY26. March utilisation was slightly above 20%. Tariff rises 5% from April.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Qatar supply to resume within 3 to 4 weeks of the conflict ending, with full supply per the annual delivery plan from around the first week of June.
Management declined to give a full-year utilisation number and asked analysts to wait until the quarter ends; April and May were said to be at about the March level.
FY27 capex is about INR 9,000 crore, of which about INR 7,500 crore is for the petchem project (plus or minus 10%); FY28 capex is guided at about 10% higher.
Dividend: a final dividend of INR 3 per share was recommended, and the endeavour is to maintain the dividend level in absolute terms.
Two new supply contracts (Exxon, about 0.5 mt in April; Equinor, first cargo for Performance Chemiserve on 12 May) add roughly 1 million tonnes in FY27.
capex_capacity: Dahej capacity expanded from 17.5 to 22.5 MMTPA; the entire expansion is commissioned and capitalised except one facility. INR 390 crore was capitalised in Q4 and about INR 100 crore is expected in Q1 FY27.

FY27 capex about INR 9,000 crore: petchem about INR 7,500 crore, third jetty about INR 600 crore, Gopalpur about INR 300-400 crore, a fifth small-scale LNG plant at Kochi about INR 70 crore, with the remainder routine.
Cash capex in FY26 was INR 2,511 crore; provisioning means some FY27 capex will sit in provisions at year end. Petchem spend in FY26 was about INR 1,650 crore.
Storage: two tanks at Gopalpur (board-approved) and one additional tank at Kochi at about INR 1,200 crore. Additional Dahej tanks (3-4) are only at the land-scouting stage with no immediate plan.
The Kochi-Bangalore pipeline is expected in the first half of FY27, which management said will raise Kochi utilisation in FY28.
demand_pricing: Spot LNG prices spiked to about $25/mmBtu after the crisis and were moving to $15-17 at the time of the call; March spot purchase prices were about $20.
Third-party cargoes from GAIL, IOCL, BPCL, GSPC and Torrent lifted utilisation from March levels; the spot cargoes are brought in by capacity holders, not by Petronet itself.
Gujarat Gas guided about 5-6 mmscmd of additional demand from May for the Morbi market; management said that depends on whether it is sustained.
Use-or-pay dues of INR 630 crore relating to CY2022 were collected in Q4, and a provision was reversed in the P&L (about INR 496 crore net of provisions for CY23 and CY24 and a INR 13 crore waiver).
Inventory gain of INR 95 crore and trading gain of INR 118 crore were recorded.

qa_highlights.question: How did March volumes look, and how much volume is at risk in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej March utilisation was about 53% and Kochi slightly above 20%. Management said utilisation has been rising since early April through third-party cargoes, but April and May are at about the March level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Qatar supply disruption affecting the trains that supply Petronet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in constant contact with QatarEnergy and expects supply to resume within 3-4 weeks of the conflict ending, with no impact on the trains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakup and FY28 expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 9,000 crore, with petchem about INR 7,500 crore, third jetty about INR 600 crore and Gopalpur about INR 300-400 crore. FY28 is guided at about 10% more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Kochi tariff hike and the storage plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The Kochi tariff rises 5% from April. Storage plans are Gopalpur (two tanks) and one additional tank at Kochi at about INR 1,200 crore; Dahej expansion depends on land.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IndAS impacts for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 gross-margin impact is +INR 119 crore, forex loss INR 91 crore, depreciation INR 77 crore and lease interest INR 59 crore. For FY26 the gross-margin impact is +INR 629 crore.

risks_watch: Duration of the Gulf conflict and whether Qatari cargoes resume in June; utilisation stayed near 53% in April-May.
Whether Qatar makes up the lost volumes within FY27, as management is discussing with QatarEnergy.
Status of the Qatar SPA extension from 2028 and the DES versus FOB terms; management said no renegotiation of Incoterms is needed.
Force majeure treatment of time-charter costs for March onwards, which management said are not payable.
Kochi-Bangalore pipeline timing and its effect on FY28 Kochi utilisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term recovery and the dividend, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term volumes. Management repeatedly declined to give utilisation or contract-level numbers and pointed analysts to the quarter-end.
key_quotes: I am pleased to share that the company has delivered a strong financial and operational performance during the current quarter, despite the challenging external environment arising from the ongoing crisis in the Gulf region.
So, we should not be unnecessarily be pessimistic about the entire year.
